1. f7 {The king's bishop's pawn, one move. (a) NOTE: In this position, the white ought to look
for an opportunity of changing the queen against the queen; and the black, to prevent that
exchange, must keep the king at a distance from the adverse king, in order to be the better
enabled to give perpetual check.} Qg5+ {The queen gives check, at her king's knight's fourth
square.} 2. Qg6 {The queen covers the check.} Qe5+ {The queen gives check, at her king's fourth
square.} 3. Kg8 {The king, at the adverse king's knight's square. (b) NOTE: He can no more give
you check, without losing the game; but he may hinder your pawn from making a queen.} Qd5 {The
queen, at her fourth square.} 4. Kh7 {The king, at the adverse king's rook's second square.}
Qh1+ {The queen gives check, at the adverse king's rook's square.} 5. Qh6 {The queen covers the
check.} Qe4+ {The queen gives check, at the adverse king's fourth square.} 6. Kg8 {The king, at
the adverse king's knight's square.} Qg4+ {The queen gives cheek, at the adverse king's knight's
fourth square.} 7. Qg7 {The queen covers the check.} Qe6 {The queen, at her king's third square.
GAME Won with a QUEEN, against a Pawn near making a QUEEN.} *
